newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares cash in gains after hitting new high.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares cash in gains after hitting new high.

text.p: Norwegian shares submitted to profit-taking on Wednesday and brokers said there was still room to the downside despite the generally bullish sentiment.
The Total share index slid 0.37 percent, or just over three points, to 881.45 points after setting another all-time high just after the open of trade at 885.01 points.
Turnover was a moderate 644 million crowns.
"We saw some early profit taking as with other markets in Europe. The U.S. CPI figures came out as expected and some buying coming back into the market before the close," said one dealer.
"New York will set the pace tomorrow. There's still room for a small correction but overall sentiment is bullish."
Diversified industrial giant Norsk Hydro retreated four crowns in 118 million crowns of business with some players choosing reduce their stake ahead of the group's third quarter profits next Monday.
Hydro has already said it expects weak results in its aluminium division and could take a loss due to a bad performing field in the oil and gas business.
"Investors are being careful on Hydro before the numbers, they don't want to be too long," commented one broker.
